content:
London-based fintech startup Acorda, which
helps payment providers detect and prevent scams, has raised £1.8 million in a
pre-seed funding round led by Concept Ventures, with participation from NFG Ventures and angel investors with experience at Monzo, Revolut, Coinbase and
OakNorth Bank.

Founded in October 2026 by former Monzo scam
prevention team members Jhamat Mahbubani, Sam Kelsey and Robert Parrish, Acorda
is developing a platform that enables payment providers to share risk
information and identify potential scams before transactions take place.

During three years at Monzo, the founders
developed machine learning models that helped prevent millions of pounds in
scam losses. They also identified a key limitation in fraud prevention: the
lack of information about payment recipients.

While banks have detailed knowledge of their
own customers, they often have limited visibility into the individuals or
businesses receiving payments. This makes it difficult to distinguish
legitimate transactions from fraudulent ones, particularly when customers are
manipulated into transferring money to scammers. The challenge is becoming
increasingly significant as scams grow more sophisticated, partly driven by
advances in AI.

Acorda aims to address this information gap
by enabling payment providers to exchange risk signals across both sides of a
transaction. Through a single integration, the platform allows banks,
cryptocurrency exchanges and other payment providers to access additional
information to assess potential fraud without establishing separate connections
with each institution.

Jhamat Mahbubani, co-founder and CEO of
Acorda, commented:

Banks have talented engineers and data
scientists who are motivated to stop scams, but are missing the data they need.
We want to provide better data in a way that they genuinely love to use.

Acorda is already conducting trials with
three major global payment companies to demonstrate how access to shared risk
information can improve scam prevention.

The company will use the new funding to
validate its technology and demonstrate results with these initial partners
before expanding to additional payment providers.
